findings.title: C11 makes live-generation revocation a status-preserving append and does not define the required REVOKED transition
findings.contract: Every trigger, review due, or revocation must use C11. C11 says every later distinct signal on a live generation appends through RO03-RO06 without changing status. Yet RO03-RO05 cover OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, and VERIFYING only as status-preserving resurface/review-due rows; the actual revocation state changes are separate RO11-RO13 rows. No row defines an atomic append-plus-revoke result, and no contract requires or orders RO11-RO13 after C11 consumes/appends the revocation event.
adversarial_trace: Reach IN_PROGRESS under RO07 with a live purpose-bound remediation grant and child attempt.
Receive a distinct signed revocation. Section 13 requires it to use C11.
C11’s declared live-generation route is RO04, which appends the event and leaves the obligation IN_PROGRESS.

RO12 is separately triggerable by revocation, but the manifest defines neither an atomic RO04+RO12 transaction nor a mandatory durable continuation from RO04 to RO12. A literal compiler may finish the required C11 event while the obligation remains IN_PROGRESS.

The same gap exists for OPEN via RO03 versus RO11 and VERIFYING via RO05 versus RO13; a first or post-CLOSED revocation also creates OPEN via RO01/RO02 without a defined compound transition to REVOKED.
findings.impact: A revoked remediation can remain in an active status, or implementations can disagree on whether and when to fence/quiesce it. Resource keys remain blocked, but unauthorized remediation activity and nondeterministic recovery behavior are possible. This fails the round-7 requirement that revocation move or mark the obligation through a legal blocking transition.
findings.required_plan_repair: Define exact closed compound rows, or an exact transactional/mandatory queued sequence, for revocation at absent/OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/VERIFYING. The event append and transition to REVOKED must be replay-safe and ordered before any further remediation authority or effect. State how same-event replay works after the status change, and retain RO06 only for later signals once already REVOKED.
